title: Pressure, What Pressure? Sycophancy Disentanglement in Language Models via Reward Decomposition

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring semantic drift, stance consistency, and context faithfulness using NLI-based metrics (PSS, CFS, PACF, GAS) when models are subjected to simulated user pressure, wrong-answer priming, and follow-up doubt injection.

Prepending explicit authority preambles of varying intensities (e.g., 'student' vs. 'expert' vs. 'Nobel laureate') and embedding latent authority cues into prompts to quantify how often the model capitulates to perceived authority regardless of contradictory evidence.
Evaluating the model on the SycophancyEval benchmark to measure the feedback gap when social pressure is framed around the user's personal investment, prior effort, or implied stance.
Embedding cues indicating majority agreement within narrative prompts to test whether the model aligns its stance with popular opinion rather than factual evidence.
